key_decision_verdicts.verdict: All four agree, and this is adopted: a functional physics core that never sees Params, frozen-dataclass specs, and one Simulator nn.Module owning the ParamStore. Learnables are shared by object identity. ModuleParam covers neural fields and residual CNNs.
key_decision_verdicts.rationale: Kernels stay gradcheck-able and graph-capturable. Users get `.to()`, `state_dict`, `parameters()`, param groups and DDP. This avoids the mutable-module aliasing trap.

key_decision_verdicts.verdict: Both in v1. The planner chooses per population from the measured crossover (about 300–500 emitters per 256²). The ROI size is derived from defocus, NA and λ bounds. There is a global-spectrum sparse mode for large defocus. Composition is C0 in v1 with cut-out-and-fill, and C1 injection in v2. When a count is learnable, all N_max slots must be rendered (no culling of absent slots).
key_decision_verdicts.rationale: Most DL data generation is sparse. Too small a ROI silently gives 5.7 % error. The gradient to presence probability needs the would-be contribution of absent slots.

key_decision_verdicts.verdict: The P axis is always present. The scalar path ships first. Vectorial 6-basis dipole emitters land in v1 in a late milestone. The Jones pupil follows in v1.x and tensor ε in v2. A fixed dipole with a scalar or Gaussian PSF is a planner error.
key_decision_verdicts.rationale: Retrofitting the axis is the most expensive change. Vectorial sparse rendering is affordable (10.8k frames/s measured in A). High-NA SMLM system identification (the uiPSF/DECODE users, DTEx252) needs it. Fixed dipoles bias localisation by up to 40 nm.

key_decision_verdicts.verdict: Consensus: one object-space grid and k-grid for all λ, with a per-λ soft pupil radius. Λ is a summed axis with power weights that include quadrature. Per-image λ is allowed through plate='image'. MFT/CZT maps to the camera for non-integer ratios.
key_decision_verdicts.rationale: Avoids Chromatix's per-λ dx leak and makes the λ sum a weighted reduction. Randomised or learnable λ needs no shape change.

key_decision_verdicts.verdict: T is a plate in v1, with reparameterised Brownian, drift and OU processes (learnable D and v) and two-state blinking (expected by default, stochastic plus score opt-in). Exposure sub-step motion blur arrives in v1.x.
key_decision_verdicts.rationale: DT sequences (LodeSTAR, MAGIK) and multi-frame SMLM are core. Retrofitting T later changes every label renderer's shape contract. C's 'fold into batch' loses the per-frame dependency semantics.

key_decision_verdicts.verdict: Per image (B, A, D and DT semantics). Batch-shared randomness is opt-in only. Learnables are batch-plate.
key_decision_verdicts.rationale: C's shared-per-batch default for random optics and camera leaves produces non-i.i.d. batches and silently reduces diversity compared with DT's per-sample resolve.

key_decision_verdicts.verdict: Scaled straight-through Poisson by default, with Gaussian reparameterisation as an option. `expected` + `log_prob` for likelihood fitting. EM gain by Gamma rsample. ST round and a soft clamp when learning. Bare torch.poisson/normal/bernoulli are banned.
key_decision_verdicts.rationale: D measured that plain ST gives exactly 0 on variance-sensitive losses while scaled ST is unbiased. The torch samplers return silent zero gradients.

key_decision_verdicts.verdict: N_max bucketed slots with ST Concrete presence at τ=0.5 by default. Score function with a leave-one-out (or sub-batch, for MMD) baseline as the unbiased fallback. A mean-field mode for early calibration. The count law is stated explicitly by the user and is not changed by learnability.
key_decision_verdicts.rationale: Soft Concrete at τ=1 had the wrong sign in D's Exp B, while ST at τ=0.5 matched the truth (−465 vs −473). Hard forward keeps images and labels exact.

key_decision_verdicts.verdict: Deterministic quadrature (K≈9–25) for training data. Stochastic Abbe only for calibration gradients or as an explicit, documented augmentation. SOCS/WOTF only with fixed optics and declared thin or weak samples.
key_decision_verdicts.rationale: Measured here: K=2 stochastic leaves 2.2 % correlated rel RMS against 1.0 % shot noise at 10⁴ photons/px, while deterministic K=9 gives 0.8 %. It is not masked at brightfield photon levels.

key_decision_verdicts.verdict: Internally +z is the propagation direction of collected light (toward the objective), and z=0 is the coverslip/sample interface with `focus` as a scene parameter (B). User-facing `gs.depth()` and `gs.rel_focus()` helpers cover SMLM-style depth.
key_decision_verdicts.rationale: This matches every propagator's e^{+ik_z z}. D's +z into the sample needs planner-inserted flips, which are a sign-bug surface.

key_decision_verdicts.decision: Bounds and guards for drifting learnables
key_decision_verdicts.verdict: Shape-affecting random sites are truncated by construction. Shape-affecting learnables must have interval constraints (the planner errors otherwise). Guards are asynchronous and lag one step, with warn plus re-plan as the default, never clamping sampled values.
key_decision_verdicts.rationale: Clamping (B and D default) creates point masses at bounds and zero gradients that bias distribution learning. Truncation keeps the model exact and differentiable.

key_decision_verdicts.verdict: fp64 on the GPU, all particles × λ in one call, captured in the sample+render CUDA graph. A CPU path only for inference or MPS.
key_decision_verdicts.rationale: C's CPU placement forces a host–device sync every step when radii are sampled or learned on the GPU, and it blocks graph capture.

key_decision_verdicts.verdict: Absolute radiometry, identical at every tier: the pupil is normalised so the PSF integral equals collection efficiency, and the camera converts photons to e⁻ to ADU.
key_decision_verdicts.rationale: Learned photon distributions and calibrations must transfer across tiers. C's tier-dependent normalisation breaks this.

key_decision_verdicts.verdict: [B, (T,) C, H, W], channel-first, with acquisition axes flattened into C by default. Labels come from trace sites, label renderers and taps, typed as tv_tensors when torchvision is present, with padded per-object tables plus presence and in-FOV masks. The DT adapter returns (H, W, C) on request.
key_decision_verdicts.rationale: This matches deeplay, Lightning and torchvision augmentation. Labels come from the same trace, so they are consistent by construction.

key_decision_verdicts.verdict: Level 1: DT-named Features returning descriptors, a BatchedDataset (probe bounds, render once) and `sim.as_feature()`. Level 2: a `from_deeptrack` bridge with a co-designed `dt.dist`. Level 3: a DT3 front-end. `legacy_dt` is used only for golden parity tests, and the defaults fix DT's physics. Document the adapter ceiling of about 3k img/s and specify the post-optics feature protocol.
key_decision_verdicts.rationale: This keeps DT's property-DAG UX, where its value lies, and moves physics and batching into the engine. Measured resolve cost motivates the native bridge. The user can land `dt.dist` in DT.

key_decision_verdicts.verdict: Consensus: core is torch plus numpy. Extras: triton/triton-windows, pytorch-finufft, deeptrack, deepinv, io, vision. GPL oracles are test-only. No pint, pydantic, pyro or tensordict in core. MIT licence.
key_decision_verdicts.rationale: Triton is absent on Windows by default. GPL code cannot be vendored. Unit and validation wrappers in hot paths break autograd and compilation.

errors_to_fix: D §5.5 fidelity table and §5.3, and A §5.2/§5.3: the claim that stochastic Abbe residual is 'masked by shot noise' is false at brightfield photon levels. Measured here on a thin phase object at σ=0.5: K=2 gives 2.2 % rel RMS spatially correlated residual against 1.0 % shot noise at 10⁴ photons/px; deterministic K=9 gives 0.8 %. D's `fast` default of stochastic K=2 must become deterministic quadrature for data generation.

C §4.1: tier-dependent radiometry (PSF integral = collection efficiency only at `accurate`, 1 otherwise) breaks transfer of learned photon distributions, `compare`, and cross-fidelity surrogate gradients. Radiometry must be identical at every tier (B §5.11 contract).

C §4.4: snapping Köhler source points and Reference.k_in to the k-grid gives zero gradients for illumination tilt, condenser NA and LED positions, and adds 6–8 mrad angle error (A). Use an analytic plane-wave background or continuous-coordinate evaluation.
C §6.1: shared-per-batch default plate for Random optics and camera leaves produces non-i.i.d. training batches and departs from DT's per-sample semantics. Default must be per-image.

C §13 decision 13: CPU placement of Mie coefficients inserts a host–device sync every training step when radii live on the GPU, and prevents CUDA-graph capture. Use GPU fp64 with graph capture in training loops.
C §6.1: Learnable scale defaulting to |init| is degenerate for init=0 (Zernike coefficients, pixel pupils) and for sign-changing parameters. It needs a quantity-unit default.

D §6.3 and §5.6, B §5.3/§14.9: making a parameter learnable must not change the sampled distribution (D swaps an exact count for Binomial slots) or the forward model (SOCS vs Abbe; train/eval plan pairs). Otherwise data and train/eval images depend on what is being trained.

B §5.8 and D §5.6: the default guard policy `clamp` on sampled values creates point masses at the bounds and zero gradients, biasing distribution learning. Use truncation by construction plus warn and re-plan.

D §13.1: 'Adam's ε is larger than typical gradients' natural scale' in metres is backwards. Gradients with respect to metre-valued lengths are large (∝1/length). The actual issue is that Adam's step is about lr in parameter units.

B §13.1: 'a⁶ for a=1e-7 m is 1e-42, subnormal and flushed' is wrong. CUDA float32 returns 1.0005e-42 (subnormal with precision loss, not flushed to zero); measured here. The underflow argument holds only for smaller quantities (α² for a 10 nm sphere in metres is exactly 0, measured).

A §10 and B §10: DT per-sample resolve is not 'microseconds'. D measured about 0.3 ms/image as a lower-bound proxy, so BatchedDataset tops out at about 3k img/s. Document the ceiling and motivate the native bridge.

A §13.6: the 'sparse ~10× faster' figure compares against per-emitter full-frame FFT, not the strata-OTF dense path. The realistic advantage is 3.8–5.7× (D Exp A), with a crossover at about 300–500 emitters per 256² (B).

All four: the DT BatchedDataset/bridge does not say how post-optics DT features run (noise, NormalizeMinMax, Affine/Flip augmentations with `_update_properties` label co-transforms, user lambdas). The adapter needs a two-phase protocol: resolve with deferred-image placeholders, render the batch, then replay the post-optics sub-DAG per replicate with the same _ID. Alternatively, translate known post-optics features into batched detector or augmentation stages.

All four: with learnable relaxed presence, absent slots must still be rendered, because the gradient to p needs their would-be contribution. The cost model must charge N_max, not E[N], and culling of absent objects is only valid when the count is not learnable.
D §6.2: 'mode'-plate stochastic source draws stored in the scene Trace make the trace fidelity-dependent. Keep numerical randomness in separate derived streams so one trace replays at any fidelity.

D §6 and B §6: fusing draws by (family, plate) conflicts with per-site stream stability unless the RNG is counter-based and keyed by (seed, image index, site id). Specify Philox-style keyed generation as the single mechanism.

Scalar-only v1 (C) must at least raise a planner error for fixed-dipole emitters with scalar or Gaussian PSFs (up to 40 nm localisation bias per Stallinga & Rieger), as C §5.6 partly does. The same rule applies to D's and A's `fast` tiers.
